lines.text: I could take five. Any more, and it would look like an army. Any fewer, and it would look like a funeral.
I'm coming. Dunn would have come. So I'm coming for both of us.
I know the capital, my lord. Its gates, its knights, its back alleys. And every tavern in it, I'm sorry to say.
I know the Order's halls, its codes and its passwords. And my sister is somewhere in that city.
And I'm coming.
You're the one person in the north they've ordered me to hand over.
Then I'll be someone else. The Remeasuring is my trade, Lucan. You'll need someone who knows every trick that Stone can play.
Tamsin disguised her as a clerk's widow. Without her glasses, Ilse walked straight into the door.
Square spectacles. No Measurer would be seen dead in square spectacles. It's perfect.
And Ash. Nobody asked Ash. Ash had never needed asking.
And I stay. Someone has to hold the threads at this end, my lord. And stop Tobin building anything that explodes.
Bram...
I'm the strongest man in Greyhollow. Two rings, officially. Go.
Fog lanterns, my lord. A whole crate. They blind the Order's lenses, and where you're going is full of lenses. Just in case.
Tobin's just-in-case had killed a frost-wyrm once. I took the crate.
That night, my wards wouldn't sleep until I hummed the old song. The one I never learned. Slow and low, like wind going round a chimney.
Lucan. That song. There's something I should have told you, a long time ago.
What?
...Your father loves you. Whatever he says. Whatever he writes.
That's what you wanted to tell me?
Yes, my lord.
It was the first time Bram had ever lied to me. I let him.
After I went up to bed, I heard him down in the hall, talking quietly to the lamp. The way you talk to someone who isn't there.
I should have told him.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter sixty, coming soon.
